title: बजेट चक्रका चरणहरू बिचको तार्किक सम्बन्ध र पुँजीगत खर्च सुधार: Logical Relation between Budget Cycle and Improvement of Capital Expenditure
nepali: आय व्ययको विवरण र बार्षिक वित्तीय योजना प्रस्तुत गर्ने इतिहास लामो छ। समयक्रमसँगै बजेटको आकार र आयतनका साथै यसको अर्थ र आधारभूत संरचनामा पनि परिवर्तन भएको छ। शुरुमा बजेटलाई एक आर्थिक बर्षको सम्भावित आय र प्रस्तावित खर्चको विवरण मानिन्थ्यो। बजेट तथा वार्षिक विकास कार्यक्रम सरकारको आर्थिक दर्शन, नीति तथा प्राथमिकताको संयन्त्र भएकाले यो जति सन्दर्भिक, वास्तविक र कार्यान्वयनयोग्य भयो त्यति नै आर्थिक सामाजिक प्राथमिकतालाई संवोधन गर्न सकिन्छ। बजेट चक्रका चरणहरुबीच तार्किक सम्बन्ध स्थापित गरेर सरकारी विनियोजनलाई नतिजामुखी बनाउँदै राज्यबाहिरका पात्रहरुको क्रियाशीलता बढाउन नेपालमा नीति संरचनाहरु भएपनि ती अपेक्षित नतिजामा पुग्ने गरी क्रियाशील भएनन्। किन बजेट प्रस्ताव र कार्यान्वयनबीच खाडल बढ्दै गयो ? बजेट व्यवस्थापनका चरणहरुमा पात्रहरुको भूमिका कसरी प्रभावकारी पार्ने भन्ने पक्षमा विश्लेषण गर्न प्रस्तुत लेख केन्द्रित रहेको छ।
american_english: The history of presenting details of income and expenditure alongside the annual financial plan is a long one. Over time, the size and volume of the budget have changed, as have its meaning and fundamental structure. Initially, the budget was regarded as a statement of the estimated income and proposed expenditure of a fiscal year. Since the budget and the annual development programme embody the government's economic philosophy, policy and priorities, the more contextual, realistic and implementable it becomes, the more effectively it can address economic and social priorities. Although Nepal has policy structures aimed at making government allocation result-oriented by establishing logical relations between the phases of the budget cycle and enhancing the activity of non-state actors, those structures did not function in a way that delivered the expected results. Why is the gap between the budget proposal and implementation widening? This article focuses on analysing how the roles of actors can be made effective across the phases of budget management.
british_english: The history of presenting a breakdown of income and expenditure alongside the annual financial plan goes back a long way. With the passage of time, the budget's size and volume have altered, as too have its meaning and its underlying structure. At the outset, the budget was seen as a statement of projected income and proposed spending for a financial year. Because the budget and the annual development programme form the government's economic philosophy, policy and priorities, the more grounded, realistic and implementable it is, the better it can address economic and social priorities. Nepal does possess policy frameworks intended to make government allocation result-oriented by forging logical links between the phases of the budget cycle and to boost the activity of non-state actors, yet these frameworks did not operate in a manner that produced the expected results. Why is the gap between the budget proposal and implementation widening? This article focuses on analysing how the roles of actors can be made effective across the phases of budget management.
australian_english: The history of setting out income and expenditure alongside the annual financial plan goes way back. Over the years the budget's size and volume have shifted, and so have its meaning and the fundamentals of how it works. At first, the budget was taken as a statement of what income was likely to come in and what spending was proposed for a financial year. Because the budget and the annual development programme are the government's economic philosophy, policy and priorities rolled into one, the more grounded, realistic and doable it is, the more it can get a handle on economic and social priorities. Nepal's got policy frameworks that are meant to make government allocation result-oriented by linking up the phases of the budget cycle and to crank up the activity of non-state actors, but they didn't deliver the results they were after. So why's the gap between the budget proposal and implementation keeps growing? This article zeroes in on analysing how actors' roles can be made effective across the phases of budget management.
informal_english: So there's been this whole practice of putting together a detailed account of income and expenditure along with the annual financial plan — and that's been going on for ages. Over the years, the budget's size and volume have changed, and so has what it means and its basic structure. At the start, the budget was basically seen as a statement of the estimated income and proposed spending for a financial year. Now, the budget and the annual development programme are what express the government's economic thinking, its policies and what it prioritises — so the more grounded, realistic and workable the budget is, the better it can take care of economic and social priorities. Nepal does have policy frameworks that are meant to make government allocation result-oriented by building logical connections between the phases of the budget cycle and by stepping up what non-state actors do, but they just didn't deliver what was expected. So why exactly is the gap between the budget proposal and implementation keeps widening? That's what this article is getting into — it focuses on analysing how actors' roles can be made effective across the phases of budget management.
